headline: 20 crore rupees and 15kg gold recovered from retired driver's home in West Bengal
summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) seized the assets during a raid on the house of a retired government bus driver in Birbhum, India.
details: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) recovered approximately 20 crore rupees in cash and 15 kg of gold bars from the house of Minar Mondal, a retired government bus driver in the Mohammad Bazar area of Birbhum, West Bengal.
The raid took place at 3:00 AM on Tuesday, following a secret tip-off. ED officials spent 11 hours searching the premises, using counting machines to tally the massive amount of cash.
Minar Mondal is a relative of stone businessman Tulu Mondal, who is known to be close to influential Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader Anubrata Mondal.
The seized assets, which were transported away in five trunks, were recovered during an investigation into illegal stone mining operations in the Birbhum district.
According to the BJP, TMC leaders and activists have been looting loot from illegal stone quarries without paying revenue to the state treasury.
The ED has questioned Minar Mondal and his son, while stone businessman Tulu Mondal remains at large.

headline: Merging banks' depositors can withdraw up to Tk 10 lakh for emergencies
summary: Bangladesh Bank has expanded withdrawal limits for depositors of five merging Islamic banks to cover medical treatment for family and other urgent needs.
details: Bangladesh Bank has decided that depositors of five merging Islamic banks can now withdraw up to Tk 10 lakh for their own medical treatment, the treatment of immediate family members, and other emergency needs.
The decision follows a previous policy where withdrawals under the central bank's special scheme were limited strictly to the depositor's own medical expenses.
The affected banks are First Security Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, Global Islami Bank, and EXIM Bank, which are merging to form Sammilito Islami Bank PLC.
The central bank board also decided to suspend the haircut system on depositors' profits, ensuring they receive profits as per shariah law.
The merging process is expected to be completed by September this year, with administrator teams of the five banks being withdrawn soon.
These banks collapsed due to large-scale irregular lending under the control of business groups linked to the previous government.
Sammilito Islami Bank will have a paid-up capital of Tk 35,000 crore, including Tk 20,000 crore provided by the government.
So far, Tk 3,887 crore has been repaid to over 822,000 depositors under the central bank's repayment scheme.

Bangladesh Bank has decided that depositors of five merging Islamic banks can now withdraw up to Tk 10 lakh for their own medical treatment, the treatment of immediate family members, and other emergency needs.

The decision follows a previous policy where withdrawals under the central bank's special scheme were limited strictly to the depositor's own medical expenses.

The affected banks are First Security Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, Global Islami Bank, and EXIM Bank, which are merging to form Sammilito Islami Bank PLC.

The central bank board also decided to suspend the haircut system on depositors' profits, ensuring they receive profits as per shariah law.

The merging process is expected to be completed by September this year, with administrator teams of the five banks being withdrawn soon.

These banks collapsed due to large-scale irregular lending under the control of business groups linked to the previous government.

Sammilito Islami Bank will have a paid-up capital of Tk 35,000 crore, including Tk 20,000 crore provided by the government.

So far, Tk 3,887 crore has been repaid to over 822,000 depositors under the central bank's repayment scheme.
